subject: PrivDeploy license conditionality + legal timeline for Order Form
messages:
From: Devon Saunders <devon.saunders@medinovo.com>
To: Connor O'Brien <connor_obrien@redwood.com>
Cc: Alicia Ruiz <procurement@medinovo.com>
Date: Sun, 25 Apr 2027 09:15:00 -0700
Subject: MSA + Order Form redlines for Private deployment

Connor —

Thanks for the call earlier. Attaching our redlines to the MSA and the Order Form for the on-prem/VPC deployment we discussed. High level asks from procurement and legal:
- Narrow the "Operator Access" clause so only Redwood personnel required for an emergency forensic snapshot or critical patching can access customer-controlled infrastructure.
- Prefer a sealed-snapshot/witness-lite approach instead of full escrow; if Redwood insists on a live operator model they want stronger audit windows and pre-agreed witness procedures.
- Limit license grant to "use of the runtime for customer workloads" and exclude derivative rights; also need clarity on retained telemetry.
- Audit requests should be scoped (90-day notice, on-site window limited to 3 business days) and redacted for PII/PHI.

We also included a proposed Exhibit B (Operator Boundary) with suggested network-level controls. Please confirm whether Redwood can accept the sealed-snapshot alternative or if you need us to move forward with on-prem operator attestations.

Attachments: MediNovo_MSA_Redlines_20270425.docx

Thanks,
Devon Saunders
Head of Platform Integrations
MediNovo Health
Phone: +1 415-555-0123

From: Connor O'Brien <connor_obrien@redwood.com>
To: Devon Saunders <devon.saunders@medinovo.com>
Cc: Alicia Ruiz <procurement@medinovo.com>, Rachel Kim <rachel_kim@redwood.com>, David Kim <david_kim@redwood.com>
Date: Sun, 25 Apr 2027 11:02:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: MSA + Order Form redlines for Private deployment

Devon —

Appreciate the detailed redlines and the Exhibit B draft. Quick note from my side as commercial lead:
- We can accept a sealed-snapshot/witness-lite flow in many cases; there are a couple of models (certain quantized weights or licensed tooling) where we need a more prescriptive operator-proof flow. I want legal to confirm the exact tradeoffs.
- Timing: customer wants go-live in mid-June; procurement asks for final contract by May 20 to allow procurement approvals.

Looping in Rachel and David to coordinate a consolidated response and to flag anything material that would push the timeline. Next steps from Redwood: Rachel will review the Exhibit and propose operator-boundary language, David will confirm audit witness window commitments, and I’ll follow up on pricing/Order Form carveouts.

Connor O'Brien
Senior Account Executive, Redwood Inference
[Attachment: Redwood_Operator_Boundary_Exhibit.pdf]

From: Rachel Kim <rachel_kim@redwood.com>
To: Connor O'Brien <connor_obrien@redwood.com>, David Kim <david_kim@redwood.com>, Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwood.com>
Cc: Devon Saunders <devon.saunders@medinovo.com>, Alicia Ruiz <procurement@medinovo.com>
Date: Mon, 26 Apr 2027 15:20:00 -07:00
Subject: RE: MSA + Order Form redlines for Private deployment

Team / Devon —

Thanks — I’ve reviewed MediNovo’s redlines and the Exhibit B. High-level legal position and proposed language edits below (summary; I’ve attached tracked redlines):

1) Operator access / sealed snapshot option:
- Proposal: Add an Exhibit C (Sealed Snapshot Protocol) as an alternative to live operator access. Exhibit C will define: scope of artefacts deposited, witness-lite procedures (remote witness via vendor-approved auditor), custody chain, and a mutually acceptable encryption key-handling flow.
- Tradeoff: Sealed snapshots require a short-forensics exercise window during restoration; for certain licensed components Redwood may require a supervised operator check to validate model integrity. We should enumerate a narrow list of components that trigger operator-assisted validation (we propose referencing a schedule of "Restricted Components").

2) License scope and derivatives:
- Hold: We will accept a customer-limited runtime license for production workloads. We cannot grant derivative model rights; will add explicit language clarifying "no license to create independent model artifacts outside of the runtime".

3) Audit and on-site windows:
- Counterproposal: 60 calendar days' notice with a 3-business-day on-site/testing window and a one-time annual remote verification step. Insist on reasonable redaction for PHI and a technical non-disclosure buffer.

4) Evidence and custody exhibit:
- Add explicit acceptance criteria for sealed snapshots (hashing algorithm, signing cert, witness attestation format). This will be Exhibit C referenced above.

Next steps: I’ve uploaded tracked redlines (attachment) and proposed Exhibit C draft. David — can you confirm whether our forensic/supervised-operator SLA carveouts are acceptable from ops/serving runtime perspective? Priyom — please prepare an engineering runbook stub to include in Exhibit C showing how the snapshot is created and validated.

Attachments: Redwood_MSA_Countertrack_20270426.docx; ExhibitC_SealedSnapshot_Draft.pdf

Regards,
Rachel Kim
Senior Counsel, Commercial Contracts
Redwood Inference

From: Liam O'Neill <liam.oneill@birchbrook-legal.com>
To: Rachel Kim <rachel_kim@redwood.com>, Connor O'Brien <connor_obrien@redwood.com>
Cc: Devon Saunders <devon.saunders@medinovo.com>, Alicia Ruiz <procurement@medinovo.com>, David Kim <david_kim@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 27 Apr 2027 08:45:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: MSA + Order Form redlines for Private deployment

Rachel / Connor —

Thanks for the quick turnaround and the Exhibit C draft. MediNovo is broadly comfortable with the sealed-snapshot approach provided we get:
- A signed witness attestation template we can rely on (to be executed remotely).
- A statement limiting operator intervention to the narrow "Restricted Components" list and a guaranteed escalation path if an integrity mismatch is discovered.
- Confirmation that audit windows will not be used to access live PHI and that any PII/PHI is handled under the existing data handling exhibit.

Procurement target is still May 20 for a complete set of final documents. Can Redwood commit to delivering the Exhibit C runbook and the signed witness template by May 6 so our internal GC can triage before procurement approval? If you can, we’ll queue the Order Form for signature immediately after that review.

Also please include a single redlined Order Form that reflects the pricing carveout for sealed-snapshot (we suggested a 7% uplift for operator-assisted restoration windows; procurement would like Redwood to confirm or adjust).

Best,
Liam O'Neill
Counsel, Birchbrook Legal (for MediNovo)
[Attachment: MediNovo_MSA_Redlines_20270425.docx]
